analysis.investment_thesis: Chalet Hotels is a capital-hungry, cyclically volatile hospitality business with a D/E of 0.73 and ROE of only 5.77% — it fails my two most non-negotiable screens. The business demonstrated its fragility in 2021 when COVID nearly wiped out revenue, and 2025's FCF turned negative (-14 Cr) even as capex surged to 969 Cr.
key_strengths: Strong promoter holding at 67.33% and stable
Revenue recovering well post-COVID with 12.8% 9-year CAGR and expanding EBITDA margins (~44%)
Operating CF strong at 950 Cr in 2025, demonstrating underlying business cash generation
key_risks: Debt/Equity of 0.73 is well above my absolute ceiling of 0.3 — borrowings still at 2,489 Cr
Net profit has been negative in 5 of 10 years; 2025 profit collapsed to 142 Cr from 278 Cr in 2024
Massive capex cycle (969 Cr in 2025, up from 42 Cr in 2022) will pile on more debt
red_flags: ROE of 5.77% is dismal — capital is not being deployed productively
FCF turned negative in 2025 despite strong OCF due to aggressive expansion spending
P/E of 28x for a business with volatile and low returns — significantly overvalued
Hospitality is highly cyclical and subject to external shocks (COVID, geopolitics, recessions)
analysis.detailed_analysis: Chalet is exactly the kind of business I struggle with: high fixed assets, cyclical demand, and a balance sheet that requires perpetual debt financing. The operating margins look impressive at 35% but ROE of 5.77% tells the real story — too much capital is tied up in real estate assets generating inadequate returns. Finance costs have consumed earnings for most of the company's history.
